speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources in the last five years, how many companies have been prosecuted for illegal discharge of wastewater into our public sewage system and how many of these have been second-time offenders and multiple repeat offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Under the Sewerage and Drainage Act, companies have to obtain Written Approvals from the Public Utilities Board (PUB) before they can discharge industrial used water or trade effluent into the sewers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Any discharge has to comply with stipulated quality requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB has a comprehensive programme in place to tackle discharge which do not comply with quality requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This consists of online sensors in the public sewerage system for effective monitoring and early detection, periodic inspections of premises as well as engagement of companies to comply with the quality requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These efforts complement the penalty framework that PUB has in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The order will be lifted only when the company has implemented remedial measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We take a serious view of illegal discharge of trade effluent into our sewers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will not hesitate to take enforcement action against companies that threaten the quality of our water supply.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have three supplementary questions regarding the levers that PUB has to use against errant companies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first is, regarding repeat offenders with multiple occasions of doing this illegal discharge, there is a very popular bakery that was charged in 2014, 2016, 2017 and 2018.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does constant surveillance actually act as a deterrent for these companies?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The companies do not seem to be caring for the reputational damage, even when the names are released to the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, is constant surveillance a deterrent at all?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is: when would approval to discharge the trade effluent be suspended or revoked for repeat offenders?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, how many times and what kind considerations does PUB have in revoking the approval?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The third question is: regarding the fines, are they adequate?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under the law, offenders can be fined up to $100,000.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But the fines for repeat offenders do not seem to exceed $20,000 so far, as reported in the press.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier, the majority actually comply with the requirements under which they can discharge trade effluent into the public sewers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But from time to time, there are some who do not comply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PUB manages about 3,500 kilometres (km) of sewers, and used water is a resource.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PUB needs to ensure that every drop of used water that goes into our water reclamation plants does not disrupt the water reclamation process.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Of course, it also takes seriously the potential impact on the environment as well as the harm, for instance, to the staff managing the water reclamation plants.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, stringent enforcement is carried out, together with a suite of measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the context of the 5,000 Written Approvals, as well as the fact that there are 3,500 km of sewers, the suite of measures, as I have said, include online sensors for early detection and unannounced onsite surveillance visits.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some of them may be required to put in, install their own online water quality monitoring sensors, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For some of these repeat offenders, we also engage them closely to try and ensure that these do not happen again.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They are also liable to imprisonment, or both.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As for the second question, I think I have answered it, which relates to when Written Approvals will be revoked.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Written Approvals will be revoked, for instance, when they discharge a dangerous or hazardous toxic substances.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First of all, we may issue an immediate stop order, so that they do not discharge dangerous toxic effluent.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Then, if they are very egregious, we will revoke the Written Approval, which means that if they want to continue business, they will have to engage the services of a licensed toxic industrial waste collector.
